curatorBrief.title: Welcome to Letter-Sound Safari!
curatorBrief.intent: Welcome kindergarten learners to their first letter-sound group: s, a, t, i, p, and n. Introduce each letter shape paired with its most common, crisp sound (/s/, /ă/, /t/, /ĭ/, /p/, /n/), emphasizing clean pronunciation without adding 'uh' (schwa) to stop consonants like /t/ and /p/.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Produce the correct, most common sound for each letter in the set when shown the grapheme: s, a, t, i, p, n, maintaining clean phonemes (/s/, /ă/, /t/, /ĭ/, /p/, /n/) without schwa.

components.title: Meet Our First Letter Sounds
components.intent: Present clear, colorful visual cards for the six letters s, a, t, i, p, and n, pairing each grapheme with a familiar starting picture (sun, apple, tent, igloo, pan, net) and phonetic sound prompt, emphasizing crisp articulation.

components.title: Listen and Say the Sounds
components.intent: Live direct instruction spoken practice focusing on learning and saying each target sound cleanly when shown the grapheme, with guided modeling and immediate supportive audio feedback.

components.title: Spot the Letter Shape
components.intent: Provide visual discrimination and letter recognition practice across s, a, t, i, p, and n so students firmly map each grapheme shape before independent vocal production.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Independently produce the most common sound for each letter in this cumulative set (s, a, t, i, p, n) when shown its grapheme, assessed without prior teacher auditory modeling.

components.title: Say the Sound Challenge
components.intent: Engage students in direct oral production: display graphemes from Group 1 (s, a, t, i, p, n) and prompt the student to produce the sound aloud into the microphone independently.

components.title: Quick Sound Match
components.intent: Untimed automaticity practice where students match displayed letterforms (s, a, t, i, p, n) to audio pronunciations and visual keyword anchors at their own pace.

finalAssessment.title: Super Sound Check!
finalAssessment.intent: Evaluate comprehensive grapheme-phoneme correspondence for all Group 1 letters (s, a, t, i, p, n) with spoken and visual recognition items confirming clean sound identification without schwa.

cards.title: Sun and Apple
cards.definition: Letter S says /s/ and letter A says /ă/.
cards.timelineContext: Our very first letters to learn.
cards.originStory: Letter S curves like a sunny snake, and letter A looks like a round apple with a stem.
cards.curiosityNote: Your mouth opens wide when you say /ă/!
cards.visualPrompt: A bright yellow smiling sun and a shiny red apple beside cheerful lower-case letters s and a, colorful preschool picture book illustration.

cards.title: Tent and Igloo
cards.definition: Letter T says /t/ and letter I says /ĭ/.
cards.timelineContext: The middle pair of sound group one.
cards.originStory: Letter T stands straight like a tall tent pole, while letter I has a cool igloo dot on top.
cards.curiosityNote: A quick /t/ sounds just like a ticking clock!
cards.visualPrompt: A cozy green camping tent next to a friendly snowy igloo with bold colorful letters t and i, inviting kindergarten storybook style.

cards.title: Pan and Net
cards.definition: Letter P says /p/ and letter N says /n/.
cards.timelineContext: The final pair of our first set.
cards.originStory: Letter P pops like a pancake in a pan, and letter N arches like an insect net.
cards.curiosityNote: Saying /n/ tickles your nose when you hum it!
cards.visualPrompt: A shiny cooking pan and a bright butterfly net sitting beside friendly lowercase letters p and n, playful preschool art style.

problems.question: Which word starts with the letter S sound?
problems.rationale: Sun begins with the /s/ sound made by the letter S. Apple begins with the /a/ sound, and turtle begins with the /t/ sound. Listening for the first sound helps learners match spoken words to their target letter.
problems.teachingNote: Have students stretch out the beginning sound like a hissing snake (/ssss/-un) while tracing the letter S in the air to link auditory and visual recognition.
successCriteria: Identify the initial /s/ sound associated with the letter S
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: What sound does the letter 'a' make?
problems.rationale: The letter 'a' makes the short /ă/ sound, which is the sound you hear at the start of the word 'apple'. The other choices are different letter sounds, such as /m/ for monkey and /s/ for snake. Thinking of an apple helps us remember the sound /ă/.
problems.teachingNote: Encourage learners to produce a crisp short /ă/ sound without adding an extra 'uh' sound at the end. Using hand motions, such as pretending to take a bite of an apple, helps reinforce the letter-sound connection.
successCriteria: Identify the short /ă/ sound produced by the letter 'a'
Distinguish the /ă/ sound from other basic letter sounds

inset.definition: The letter 'a' makes the short /ă/ sound, like at the start of apple.
inset.label: Letter Sound

problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which word starts with the /t/ sound?
problems.rationale: Tiger begins with the /t/ sound made by the letter 't'. When you say tiger, your tongue taps the roof of your mouth to make the starting sound. Pig begins with /p/ and sun begins with /s/.
problems.teachingNote: Encourage students to put their hands in front of their mouths to feel the quick puff of unvoiced air when pronouncing the clean /t/ sound, being careful not to add an 'uh' sound at the end (saying /t/ instead of 'tuh').
successCriteria: Identify the initial /t/ sound in a spoken word
Distinguish the /t/ sound from other Group 1 consonant sounds (/p/ and /s/)
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which word starts with the /s/ sound?
problems.rationale: Sun starts with the /s/ sound, making the hissing sss sound at the beginning. The words nut and nose start with the /n/ sound. That makes sun the correct match for the /s/ group.
problems.teachingNote: Have children touch their noses to feel the vibration when pronouncing /n/ compared to the blowing air of /s/ to build phonemic awareness.
successCriteria: Distinguish between initial consonant sounds /s/ and /n/
Identify a spoken word that begins with the letter sound /s/
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.statement: The letter p makes a 'puh' sound with an extra 'uh' vowel attached at the end when we say its letter sound.
problems.rationale: The letter p makes a clean 'p' sound without adding an extra 'uh' sound at the end. Adding a vowel sound like 'uh' makes blending sounds together into words much harder for beginning readers.
problems.teachingNote: Remind students to clip the sound short—just a quick puff of air for 'p' rather than 'puh'.
successCriteria: Produce the clean sound for the letter p without adding a schwa vowel
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: What starts with the letter N sound?
problems.rationale: Nest begins with the /n/ sound made by the letter N. Tiger starts with /t/ and apple starts with /a/. Connecting the letter N to the first sound in nest helps build strong phonemic awareness.
problems.teachingNote: Ensure learners pronounce a clean continuous /n/ sound rather than adding a schwa (avoid 'nuh'). Have students feel the vibration in their nose when making the /n/ sound.
successCriteria: Identify the initial /n/ sound corresponding to the letter n
Distinguish the /n/ sound from other Group 1 letter sounds like /t/ and /a/

objectives.objective:
Letter-Sound Group 1: s, a, t, i, p, n

**New Sounds Introduced:**
/s/, /ă/, /t/, /ĭ/, /p/, /n/

**Full Practice Set (Cumulative):**
s, a, t, i, p, n

**Focus:** Produce the correct, most common sound for each letter in the set when shown the grapheme (the letter shape). For example, when shown 'a', the student says /ă/ (as in 'apple'). It is crucial to teach clean sounds (e.g., a crisp /t/ sound, not "tuh").
objectives.notes: Direct oral production is tested for s, a, n, and i, but stop consonants 't' and 'p' are omitted from assessment. Visual search in letter-spotter and multiple-choice items in final-sound-check do not assess oral sound production.

objectives.objective: Independently produce the most common sound for each letter in this cumulative set, when shown its grapheme. Assess without first saying its sound: s, a, t, i, p, n.
objectives.notes: Direct grapheme-to-phoneme production is assessed for s, a, n, and i, but letters 't' and 'p' are omitted. Multiple-choice and tap-matching activities in fast-fact and final-sound-check test receptive recognition rather than sound production.

detectedConstraints.description: Evaluator constraint prevented stop consonants 't' and 'p' from being assessed via speech evaluation (unaskableLetters=["t","p"]).
Evaluator constraint restricted see_hear oral production to held sounds, omitting target letters 't' and 'p' (unaskableLetters=["t","p"]).
Items evaluate receptive vocabulary matching and multiple-choice letter recognition rather than expressive oral production of phonemes from graphemes.

coverage.summary: The lesson provides solid explicit instruction and direct spoken production practice for continuous sounds /s/, /ă/, /ĭ/, and /n/, but fails to assess the complete target set because stop consonants /t/ and /p/ are excluded by spoken evaluation constraints. Subsequent practice blocks rely on multiple-choice image and letter matching rather than oral grapheme-to-phoneme production, leaving mastery of the full six-letter set incompletely evidenced.
